title: Seabreak Systems - renewal & regional uplift check-in
summary: Quarterly renewal/check-in focused on capacity uplift, EU region onboarding, and contract term alignment. Customer asked for latency SLAs, KMS integration details, and a price matrix for a bumped commitment. Agreed to run a 2-week private pilot in eu-west and to share security docs and a tailored pricing sheet.
action_items: Jordan Miles - Send tailored pricing matrix + commitment scenarios - Due: 2026-11-10
Priya Desai - Share private onboarding checklist and runbook + estimated provisioning time - Due: 2026-11-12
Tomás Alvarez (customer) - Share org KMS requirements and contact at security - Due: 2026-11-09
Liam O'Connor - Schedule pilot kickoff and invite infra owners - Due: 2026-11-11
next_steps: AE to share pricing and contract amendment options
SE to propose EU private pilot plan (2-week scope) and benchmark targets
Security doc pack (SOC2 + KMS/HSM notes) to be shared via secure link
Pilot kickoff scheduled for week of 2026-11-15 pending paperwork
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Time: 15:00 UTC (scheduled 45 min, ran ~48)
Attendees: Jordan Miles (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood CSM), Ava Romero (Seabreak Head of ML), Diego Chen (Infra Lead), Tomás Alvarez (Security), Maya Singh (Procurement), Speaker 6 (customer)

[00:00] Jordan Miles: Hey everyone, thanks for making time, really appreciate it. quick agenda — renewal, capacity uplift, and the eu onramp. we'll go through a couple scenarios and then priya will walk through the private pilot plan. sound good?
[00:18] Ava Romero: Yep that works. we— we have some updates on usage patterns too since last quarter, so good to sync.
[00:32] Priya Desai: hi all. i can jump straight into the pilot architecture after jordan covers the commercials.
[00:40] Diego Chen: quick note, we might be joined by our network ops later but i think todays fine.
[00:47] Jordan Miles: awesome. so first, the renewal timeline— your current term rolls off 2026-12-01. you flagged wanting a bump in committed tokens and a second region in the eu. we prepared three commitment tiers in the sheet i sent last week. any immediate preferences?
[01:05] Maya Singh: maya here, procurement — we saw the sheet, thanks. question: can those tiers be time-phased? we may want a stepped commit to align with budgets.
[01:18] Jordan Miles: yes, we can do stepped commits — month-by-month ramp or quarter ramp. stepped pricing does change the per-token effective rate, of course. i'll add those rows.
[01:30] Ava Romero: from a product POV, our peak tail latency has improved since we sharded some models but we've hit spikes in eu traffic — 95th p95 goes up to 420ms which is a bit high for live chat. is there an SLA guarantee for latency if we move to eu-private?
[01:50] Priya Desai: short answer: we offer latency SLO targets for Dedicated and Private tiers; hosted has best-effort. for private/VPC we can target p99 < 600ms and p95 typically in the 120-220ms band depending on model and sequence length. need to confirm for your specific model mix — i'll capture the sample sequences.
[02:08] Tomás Alvarez: quick interruption — what about fallback behavior? if the EU cluster is saturated do you failover to US or drop requests? we have data residency restraints so that matters.
[02:22] Priya Desai: good point. policy can be set to two behaviors: strict region-only (reject/fail) or soft-fallback to a compatible EU-allowed variant in another cluster (we do token level redirection but need you to opt in). for strict residency we keep requests internal and queue/break.
[02:38] Diego Chen: we will want strict region-only for regulatory pages; however for non-sensitive UX we could allow a fallback. is that per-route?
[02:47] Priya Desai: yes per-route. you can tag endpoints as resident-required.
[02:52] Jordan Miles: procurement and security items — maya, tomás — any gating conditions we should be aware of for contracting and KMS?
[03:00] Maya Singh: yes. we need customer-managed KMS, and we need to see the supported HSM vendors. also length of log retention; our compliance team requires 7 years for audit logs.
[03:12] Tomás Alvarez: and SOC2 type II plus ISO docs please. also, we have a checklist for third-party access and RBAC.
[03:20] Liam O'Connor: we'll share the compliance pack. redwood supports bring-your-own-KMS for Private and Dedicated; we have a list of supported HSMs. retention windows are configurable — we'll note the 7-year ask as a follow-up.
[03:34] Ava Romero: ditto — can we get a run of perf numbers for our largest model at 2k context? the p95 shift is surprising and we want baseline numbers in eu-region.
[03:46] Priya Desai: yes i can run a short benchmark. recommended is to run with the same tokenization and prompts. we'd like a small eval set from you — 50-100 examples representative of tail cases.
[03:58] Ava Romero: we'll prepare that.
[04:02] Jordan Miles: commercially — if you commit to the Tier B (1.5x tokens) we can offer a blended rate with a 12-month term and a 10% discount + free pilot credits. if you prefer shorter term we can do 6 months with slightly higher rate.
[04:16] Maya Singh: can you put the blended model in a row with stepped ramp over three quarters? budgeting likes that.
[04:23] Jordan Miles: yeah that's doable, i'll add stepped ramp rows and line items for eu-private provisioning cost.
[04:30] Speaker 6: um, small note — are there any egress charges tied to region-to-region fallback? we've got cloud egress concerns.
[04:38] Liam O'Connor: good call — fallback cross-region may incur egress if payloads are moved cross-cloud boundaries. if we keep it within the same cloud and region family egress is minimal; we'll document the scenarios.
[04:49] Priya Desai: moving into pilot scope — propose a 2-week private pilot in eu-west (eu-west-1 cluster), with the following: provision a private VPC, BYOK KMS integration, 2 dedicated nodes sized for your peak qps, and a pre-defined eval set for latency and correctness checks. we'll also enable prefix caching for common prompts to improve cold-starts.
[05:15] Diego Chen: what provisioning lead time are we looking at? we have a big marketing launch mid-december so need eu-ready by early dec.
[05:24] Priya Desai: standard private provisioning is 10-14 business days, but for pilots we can fast-track to ~5-7 business days if we have approvals and the KMS handshake done.
[05:36] Tomás Alvarez: what does the KMS handshake entail? network peering? cert exchange?
[05:42] Priya Desai: we do an HSM public key exchange and validate IAM roles; network peering is optional depending on whether you want dedicated link or managed tunneling. we'll send the cryptographic spec.
[05:54] Ava Romero: and the pilot — will it be metered or counted against our commit?
[05:58] Jordan Miles: pilot credits are separate and won't count against the commit. if pilot transitions to production early we can pro-rate.
[06:05] Maya Singh: about contract language — any flexibility on termination notice if we do a 12-month year?
[06:12] Jordan Miles: typical is 60 days notice but we can discuss mid-term options; for stepped ramps we may include a review clause at month 6.
[06:20] Speaker 6: question on observability: does redwood provide token-level breakdowns per route and per model? we want to attribute cost to product teams.
[06:30] Liam O'Connor: yes per-route dashboards and token attribution exist in the console. you can export per-token logs and cost allocation tags.
[06:36] Diego Chen: will the console expose KV cache hit rates? that's critical for our cost tuning.
[06:41] Priya Desai: yes cache metrics, batch sizes, latency percentiles, and failure counts are exposed. we'll show screenshots in the onboarding runbook.
[06:50] Jordan Miles: ok, any blockers on your side for moving forward with pilot sign-up?
[06:55] Ava Romero: main block is security signoff and KMS details. after that infra can approve.
[07:02] Tomás Alvarez: and procurement needs the pricing sheet with stepped ramp rows.
[07:08] Jordan Miles: understood. i'll send a tailored pricing matrix.
[07:12] Priya Desai: for the benchmarking, can you share the 50-100 tail cases by Monday? that helps us run the pilot with the right load shape.
[07:20] Ava Romero: yes we aim for monday.
[07:22] Maya Singh: procurement will need the contract amendments; who is the contact for legal on your side?
[07:28] Jordan Miles: legal contact is karen lee (redwood legal); i'll intro by email and cc maya.
[07:34] Speaker 6: also, any constraints on model updates during pilot? we want to test our forked model variant.
[07:40] Priya Desai: model pinning is supported; we can pin the pilot to your specific model hash and then we can open a rollout window for updates. for performance tests, pinning is recommended.
[07:51] Diego Chen: moderately off-topic — do you support quantized variants to reduce cost? we've been exploring int8 on edge for smaller LLMs.
[07:59] Priya Desai: yes we have quantization recommendations; Redwood Optimize will suggest quant profiles and expected cost/latency tradeoffs per model. we can include an initial quantization plan.
[08:10] Jordan Miles: i'll add Redwood Optimize notes to the follow-up.
[08:14] Liam O'Connor: quick note on SLAs — we'll share the SLA annex for Dedicated/Private and the credits table.
[08:21] Tomás Alvarez: perfect.
[08:23] Jordan Miles: any final questions?
[08:27] Maya Singh: procurement — can you also confirm invoicing cadence and PO workflow? we prefer quarterly invoices to map to our finance cycles.
[08:35] Jordan Miles: quarterly works; we'll reflect that in the quote.
[08:39] Ava Romero: great.
[08:41] Jordan Miles: ok, recap and next steps — quick: 1) Jordan will share tailored pricing w/ stepped ramp rows and quarterly invoice options (due 11/10). 2) Priya will share pilot runbook, provisioning checklist, and will schedule the provisioning window (due 11/12). 3) Tomás will send KMS requirements and security contact (due 11/09). 4) Liam will schedule pilot kickoff meeting and invite infra (due 11/11). 5) Customer to provide 50-100 eval prompts (due 11/08).
[09:10] Speaker 6: sounds good, thanks.
[09:13] Jordan Miles: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email and share the secure links to the SOC2 docs and KMS spec. expect an intro to legal and the quote in the next 48 hours.
[09:24] Call end.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker mislabels (Speaker 6 appears generic), filler words and run-on sentences preserved. Some acronyms may be transcribed imperfectly (HSM noted correctly but specific vendor names may be fuzzy).

References shared during the call:
- Pricing sheet (internal link): https://redwood.ai/links/pricing-seabreak-11-05 (private)
- Pilot runbook draft: https://redwood.ai/links/pilot-runbook-eu (internal)
- Compliance pack (SOC2, ISO): https://redwood.ai/secure/soc2-iso-pack (access-controlled)

End transcript.
